records.title: Precalculus: Functions, Models, and Change
records.description: A continuous Precalculus course built around functions, multiple representations, exact reasoning, modeling, and change.
records.label: Course map
keywords: A continuous Precalculus course built around functions, multiple representations, exact reasoning, modeling, and change.

records.title: Algebra and Function Readiness
records.description: A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score.

records.title: Functions and Multiple Representations
records.description: An input is supplied to a relationship, an output is determined by it, and parameters remain fixed for one selected model.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: An input is supplied to a relationship, an output is determined by it, and parameters remain fixed for one selected model.

records.title: Transformations and Function Operations
records.description: A parent function is a convenient reference member identified by domain, range, symmetry, endpoints, asymptotes, and rate patterns.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: A parent function is a convenient reference member identified by domain, range, symmetry, endpoints, asymptotes, and rate patterns.

records.title: Composition, Inverses, and Modeling
records.description: Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first.

records.title: Polynomial Functions
records.description: Power functions f(x)=ax^p connect positive, negative, and fractional exponent behavior.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: Power functions f(x)=ax^p connect positive, negative, and fractional exponent behavior.

records.title: Rational Functions
records.description: A rational function P/Q excludes every real input where the original denominator Q is zero.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: A rational function P/Q excludes every real input where the original denominator Q is zero.

records.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
records.description: Constant first differences indicate additive linear change; constant ratios indicate multiplicative exponential change.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: Constant first differences indicate additive linear change; constant ratios indicate multiplicative exponential change.

records.title: Systems, Matrices, and Multivariable Models
records.description: A system solution satisfies every equation simultaneously and appears graphically as a common intersection.
records.label: Unit map
keywords: A system solution satisfies every equation simultaneously and appears graphically as a common intersection.

records.title: Readiness diagnostic and routing
records.description: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.

A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use readiness diagnostic and routing to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Equation and inequality repair
records.description: Classify and solve common equation and inequality families while distinguishing reversible steps from candidate-generating steps.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Classify and solve common equation and inequality families while distinguishing reversible steps from candidate-generating steps.

Equation solving identifies inputs that make a statement true; inequality solving identifies an interval or union of inputs. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use equation and inequality repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Factoring and polynomial structure repair
records.description: Recognize and apply the principal factoring structures needed for polynomial-function analysis.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Recognize and apply the principal factoring structures needed for polynomial-function analysis.

Factoring rewrites a polynomial sum as a product whose factors reveal zeros, multiplicities, and sign behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use factoring and polynomial structure repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational expressions and restrictions repair
records.description: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.

A rational expression is a quotient, so every original denominator zero is excluded even when a common factor cancels. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational expressions and restrictions repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Radicals and rational exponents repair
records.description: Move among radical and rational-exponent forms, simplify exact values, and reject extraneous candidates.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Move among radical and rational-exponent forms, simplify exact values, and reject extraneous candidates.

Even roots require nonnegative radicands and the principal square root is nonnegative, so sqrt(x^2)=|x|. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use radicals and rational exponents repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential and logarithmic algebra repair
records.description: Apply exponent and logarithm laws, convert between inverse forms, and solve basic equations with valid domains.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Apply exponent and logarithm laws, convert between inverse forms, and solve basic equations with valid domains.

Exponent laws describe repeated multiplication, while logarithms reverse exponentiation. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential and logarithmic algebra repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Function notation and graph reading repair
records.description: Evaluate functions, solve output conditions, and read domain, range, intercepts, extrema, and intervals from graphs.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Function notation and graph reading repair
Evaluate functions, solve output conditions, and read domain, range, intercepts, extrema, and intervals from graphs.

Function notation f(a) asks for one output, while f(x)=k asks for every input that produces the output k. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use function notation and graph reading repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Mixed readiness synthesis
records.description: Select methods across prerequisite strands, justify restrictions, and communicate exact and approximate results.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Select methods across prerequisite strands, justify restrictions, and communicate exact and approximate results.

A complete solution identifies the mathematical object, states restrictions, selects a method, carries out the work, and interprets the result. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use mixed readiness synthesis to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Quantities, variables, and dependency
records.description: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

An input is supplied to a relationship, an output is determined by it, and parameters remain fixed for one selected model. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use quantities, variables, and dependency to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Relations and functions
records.description: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

A relation is a function when every allowed input has exactly one output. Several inputs may share an output. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use relations and functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Function notation, evaluation, and solving
records.description: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

The notation f(x) names the output of function f at input x; it is not multiplication. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use function notation, evaluation, and solving to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Words, tables, graphs, and formulas
records.description: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

Words define quantities and assumptions, tables show selected pairs, graphs reveal global behavior, and formulas support exact calculation. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use words, tables, graphs, and formulas to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Domain from formulas
records.description: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

The real domain is the intersection of every input condition imposed by denominators, even roots, logarithms, and nested functions. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use domain from formulas to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Domain from context
records.description: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

The algebraic domain states where a formula is defined; the contextual domain states where its inputs are meaningful for the model. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use domain from context to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Range and global graph behavior
records.description: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

A graph reveals range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of change. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use range and global graph behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Piecewise-defined functions
records.description: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

A piecewise function uses different rules on nonoverlapping parts of one domain. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use piecewise-defined functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Average rate of change
records.description: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

Average rate of change from a to b is [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a), the slope of the secant line through the endpoint values. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use average rate of change to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Function representation and modeling studio
records.description: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

A model is a deliberately simplified function used to answer a question; it is not the real system itself. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use function representation and modeling studio to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Parent-function atlas
records.description: Recognize benchmark function families by domain, range, symmetry, intercepts, end behavior, and rate patterns.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Recognize benchmark function families by domain, range, symmetry, intercepts, end behavior, and rate patterns.

A parent function is a convenient reference member identified by domain, range, symmetry, endpoints, asymptotes, and rate patterns. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use parent-function atlas to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Coordinate mappings and transformation logic
records.description: Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.

A graph transformation is a coordinate map from a point (u,v) on the parent to a point on the transformed graph. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use coordinate mappings and transformation logic to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Vertical translations
records.description: Analyze how adding a constant outside a function changes outputs, range, intercepts, extrema, and asymptotes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze how adding a constant outside a function changes outputs, range, intercepts, extrema, and asymptotes.

Adding k outside a function changes every output by k and moves the graph vertically. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use vertical translations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Horizontal translations
records.description: Analyze how replacing x by x-h changes input locations, domain, intercepts, extrema, and vertical asymptotes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze how replacing x by x-h changes input locations, domain, intercepts, extrema, and vertical asymptotes.

Replacing x by x-h relocates every input feature h units to the right. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use horizontal translations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Reflections and symmetry
records.description: Reflect function graphs across coordinate axes and connect reflection rules with even and odd symmetry.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Reflect function graphs across coordinate axes and connect reflection rules with even and odd symmetry.

The graph of -f(x) reflects across the x-axis; f(-x) reflects across the y-axis. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use reflections and symmetry to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Vertical and horizontal scaling
records.description: Distinguish output scaling from input scaling and determine the resulting stretches, compressions, domains, and ranges.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Distinguish output scaling from input scaling and determine the resulting stretches, compressions, domains, and ranges.

Multiplying outputs scales vertically; replacing x by cx divides horizontal coordinates by c. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use vertical and horizontal scaling to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Combined transformations
records.description: Analyze and graph functions with several transformations by tracking inputs, outputs, and key features.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze and graph functions with several transformations by tracking inputs, outputs, and key features.

Combined transformations are governed by one coordinate map rather than a memorized drawing order. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use combined transformations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Sums and differences of functions
records.description: Add and subtract functions pointwise, determine the common domain, and interpret combined outputs.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Add and subtract functions pointwise, determine the common domain, and interpret combined outputs.

Function sums and differences combine outputs at the same input. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use sums and differences of functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Products and quotients of functions
records.description: Multiply and divide functions pointwise while analyzing zeros, restrictions, and combined graph behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Multiply and divide functions pointwise while analyzing zeros, restrictions, and combined graph behavior.

Product functions multiply outputs; quotient functions divide outputs and exclude every denominator-function zero. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use products and quotients of functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Reconstructing formulas from transformed graphs
records.description: Use parent-family features, transformations, and one or more data points to construct and verify a function formula.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use parent-family features, transformations, and one or more data points to construct and verify a function formula.

Visible graph features determine a parameterized family form; one additional point often determines the remaining scale. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use reconstructing formulas from transformed graphs to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Composition as sequential processing
records.description: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use composition as sequential processing to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Composition from formulas
records.description: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

Formula composition replaces every occurrence of the outer variable with the complete inner expression. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use composition from formulas to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Composition from tables and graphs
records.description: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

Composition from tables or graphs uses two successive input-output readings. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use composition from tables and graphs to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Domains of composite functions
records.description: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

The domain of f(g(x)) requires x to be allowed by g and g(x) to be allowed by f. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use domains of composite functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: One-to-one functions
records.description: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

A one-to-one function gives each output at most one input, making reverse assignment possible. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use one-to-one functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Constructing inverse functions
records.description: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

An inverse function reverses input and output roles; it is not the reciprocal 1/f. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use constructing inverse functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Graphs and verification of inverses
records.description: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

Inverse functions undo each other in both composition orders and reflect across y=x. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use graphs and verification of inverses to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Domain restrictions and radical inverses
records.description: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

Even roots require nonnegative radicands and the principal square root is nonnegative, so sqrt(x^2)=|x|. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use domain restrictions and radical inverses to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Model construction and validation
records.description: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

A model is a deliberately simplified function used to answer a question; it is not the real system itself. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use model construction and validation to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Power functions and dominant behavior
records.description: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

Power functions f(x)=ax^p connect positive, negative, and fractional exponent behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use power functions and dominant behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Polynomial functions, degree, and leading term
records.description: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Polynomial functions, degree, and leading term
Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

A polynomial is a finite sum of nonnegative integer powers, and its leading term eventually dominates. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use polynomial functions, degree, and leading term to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: End behavior
records.description: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

Polynomial end behavior is determined by degree parity and leading coefficient sign. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use end behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Zeros, factors, and intercepts
records.description: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

For a polynomial, P(r)=0, factor x-r, and intercept (r,0) describe the same feature. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use zeros, factors, and intercepts to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Multiplicity and sign behavior
records.description: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

Multiplicity is the exponent of a repeated zero factor and controls local sign behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use multiplicity and sign behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Graph construction from structure
records.description: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

A structural polynomial sketch begins with ends, zeros, multiplicities, signs, and selected values. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use graph construction from structure to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Turning points and local versus global behavior
records.description: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Turning points and local versus global behavior
Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

A turning point changes the graph from increasing to decreasing or the reverse. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use turning points and local versus global behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Intermediate Value reasoning and root bounds
records.description: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Intermediate Value reasoning and root bounds
Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

Polynomial continuity guarantees that every intermediate output between P(a) and P(b) occurs. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use intermediate value reasoning and root bounds to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Polynomial division
records.description: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

Polynomial division produces quotient and remainder satisfying P=DQ+R. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use polynomial division to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Remainder and factor theorems
records.description: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

The remainder on division by x-c is P(c), and x-c is a factor exactly when P(c)=0. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use remainder and factor theorems to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational-root candidates and root search
records.description: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

The Rational Root Theorem produces a finite list of possible rational zeros p/q. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational-root candidates and root search to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Complex zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
records.description: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Complex zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

A degree-n polynomial has n complex zeros counted with multiplicity. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use complex zeros and the fundamental theorem of algebra to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Building polynomial models and finding numerical roots
records.description: Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Building polynomial models and finding numerical roots
Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.

A polynomial model can be built from zeros, multiplicities, end behavior, and one scale-setting condition. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use building polynomial models and finding numerical roots to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational functions and their domains
records.description: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

A rational function P/Q excludes every real input where the original denominator Q is zero. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational functions and their domains to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes
records.description: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes
Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

A common factor creates a removable discontinuity: the original function follows the simplified curve but omits one point. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Vertical asymptotes and local behavior
records.description: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

An uncancelled denominator zero often creates a vertical asymptote with unbounded one-sided behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use vertical asymptotes and local behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Horizontal asymptotes and end behavior
records.description: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

Horizontal asymptotes describe rational end behavior through leading-degree comparison. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use horizontal asymptotes and end behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Slant and polynomial asymptotes
records.description: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

Polynomial division reveals a nonhorizontal asymptote when a rational numerator has higher degree. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use slant and polynomial asymptotes to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Intercepts and sign charts
records.description: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

A rational function has constant sign between numerator zeros and denominator zeros. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use intercepts and sign charts to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Complete rational graph construction
records.description: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

A complete rational graph combines domain, holes, vertical and end asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected points. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use complete rational graph construction to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational equations and function intersections
records.description: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

Rational intersections satisfy f(x)=g(x), but denominator clearing creates candidates that must be checked in the original domains. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational equations and function intersections to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational inequalities
records.description: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

Rational inequalities are solved by critical-value sign intervals rather than unsafe cross multiplication. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational inequalities to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Variation and rational models
records.description: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

Variation language describes direct, inverse, joint, and combined proportional structure. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use variation and rational models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Partial-fraction structure
records.description: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

Partial fractions rewrite a proper rational function as a sum of simpler components determined by denominator factors. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use partial-fraction structure to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Additive versus multiplicative change
records.description: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.

Constant first differences indicate additive linear change; constant ratios indicate multiplicative exponential change. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use additive versus multiplicative change to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential functions and parameters
records.description: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.

In f(x)=ab^x, a is f(0) and b is the one-step output multiplier. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential functions and parameters to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential transformations
records.description: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.

Transformed exponentials use the general input-output mapping, with horizontal asymptote y=k. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential transformations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Growth and decay models
records.description: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.

Exponential models can be written from an initial value and rate, multiplier, doubling time, or half-life. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use growth and decay models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Compound interest and effective rate
records.description: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.

Periodic compounding uses A=P(1+r/n)^(nt), where r/n is the periodic rate and nt counts periods. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use compound interest and effective rate to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Continuous growth and the number e
records.description: Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Continuous growth and the number e
Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.

The number e arises from the limit of increasingly frequent proportional compounding. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use continuous growth and the number e to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential regression and residuals
records.description: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.

Exponential regression estimates a repeated-change model from imperfect data, and residuals measure observed minus predicted output. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential regression and residuals to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logistic and bounded growth
records.description: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.

A logistic model grows rapidly at first and then slows toward a carrying capacity K. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logistic and bounded growth to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithms as inverse functions
records.description: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.

log_b(y)=x exactly when b^x=y; a logarithm is the exponent needed to produce a positive output. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithms as inverse functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithmic graphs and transformations
records.description: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.

A transformed logarithm has a vertical input boundary where its argument equals zero. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithmic graphs and transformations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithm laws
records.description: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.

Logarithm laws convert products to sums, quotients to differences, and powers to coefficients. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithm laws to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Solving exponential equations
records.description: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.

Exponential equations place the unknown in an exponent and are solved by common bases, logarithms, substitution, or numerical methods. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use solving exponential equations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
records.description: Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.

A logarithmic equation must be solved inside the original positive-argument domain. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems as intersections and models
records.description: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

A system solution satisfies every equation simultaneously and appears graphically as a common intersection. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems as intersections and models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Nonlinear systems
records.description: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

A nonlinear system contains at least one curved relation and may have zero, one, or several intersections. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use nonlinear systems to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
records.description: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

A system of inequalities describes the intersection of several shaded solution regions. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems of inequalities and feasible regions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems in three variables
records.description: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

A linear equation in three variables describes a plane, and a system seeks their common point, line, plane, or empty intersection. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems in three variables to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Matrix notation and operations
records.description: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

A matrix is a rectangular array whose dimensions record row and column counts. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use matrix notation and operations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Augmented matrices and row operations
records.description: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

An augmented matrix records a linear system in a fixed variable order. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use augmented matrices and row operations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Gaussian elimination and echelon form
records.description: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

Gaussian elimination creates row-echelon form by clearing entries below successive pivots. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use gaussian elimination and echelon form to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
records.description: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

Reduced row-echelon form has pivot ones that are the only nonzero entries in their columns. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use gauss-jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices
records.description: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

The determinant of a square matrix detects invertibility and geometric area scaling. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Linear transformations and multivariable modeling
records.description: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.

A matrix transformation sends the standard basis vectors to its columns, determining the image of every vector. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use linear transformations and multivariable modeling to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.
